brief.headline: Push for a ₹23.53/KG discount to the India export benchmark — we pay 55% above market, and we're 1.38% of their revenue.

priceAsk.summary: Request a stepped price reduction toward the India export unit value of ₹42.95/kg for dextrose
priceAsk.target: ₹42.95/kg (India export unit value) versus our current ₹66.48/KG — a ₹23.53/KG gap
priceAsk.basis: We currently pay ₹66.48/KG while the India export benchmark sits at ₹42.95/kg. That's a 54.7% premium over the market line. Even a partial move toward that benchmark unlocks meaningful savings on our ₹15.03 Cr annual spend.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to move from 30 Days After Receipt to immediate payment in exchange for a portion of the price concession
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹1.24 Cr working capital currently tied up; accelerating payment gives them cash against their ₹226.98 Cr debt load

brief.financialLeverage: Sayaji runs a 1.1% net margin and 4.9% EBITDA margin with a leveraged balance sheet of 2.37x debt-to-equity. Their health score is D (17/100), signaling tight liquidity. However, our ₹15.03 Cr represents 1.38% of their ₹1087.88 Cr revenue — we're a volume anchor they cannot afford to lose. The thin margin means a brutal price squeeze risks supply continuity, but their debt burden (₹226.98 Cr) makes faster payment very attractive. Use volume commitment and payment acceleration as the lever, not a margin-crushing discount demand.

evidence.point: We pay ₹66.48/KG while the India export unit value for dextrose is ₹42.95/kg
Our annual spend of ₹15.03 Cr is 1.38% of their ₹1087.88 Cr revenue — we are a meaningful customer
evidence.figure: Our spend: ₹15.03 Cr; Their revenue: ₹1087.88 Cr; Share: 1.38%

evidence.point: Sayaji operates on a razor-thin 1.1% net margin
They carry ₹226.98 Cr in debt at 2.37x debt-to-equity, making cash flow a priority
Their financial health is distressed at D (17/100)
Accelerating payment from 30 days frees ₹1.24 Cr of our working capital and gives them immediate cash
evidence.figure: Working capital freed if 30 Day: ₹1.24 Cr

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: Listed starch & polyol maker with C (56/100) health and ₹2359.06 Cr revenue — established dextrose supplier, stronger balance sheet than Sayaji

alternates.name: Sanstar Ltd
alternates.why: Recently-listed maize-derivatives specialist with B (63/100) health and ₹821.13 Cr revenue — growing dextrose capacity, significantly healthier financials

alternates.name: Roquette India Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Indian arm of global starch major with ₹2898.05 Cr revenue — pharma-grade dextrose, premium but very reliable for critical supply security

risks: Their D (17/100) health score and 1.1% margin mean aggressive price pressure could trigger supply disruption — balance the ask with volume commitment
We are already at the best price we pay (₹66.48/KG) across all our dextrose suppliers, so any concession sets a new internal benchmark
High debt load (2.37x D/E) and thin margins make Sayaji a continuity watch — qualify Gulshan or Sanstar as a second source in parallel
If they cannot move on price, the ₹1.24 Cr working-capital opportunity from payment terms may be the only tangible win available
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership and the ₹15.03 Cr volume we place with you — today I'd like to talk about closing the gap between our ₹66.48/KG and the ₹42.95/kg India export benchmark, and how faster payment might help us both.
